title: Capture an executable price: opening and closing, for every market the lab originates
problem: There is no market line anywhere in this project, so the difference column is blank, the staking table is empty, and no reward can be justified. Everything downstream of a price is currently uncomputable.
evidence: nfl.com returns 404 at /odds/ (CP-NFL-ODDS-ABSENT). The price store holds 0 rows for 78 registered markets. 0 strategies are live and 0 are provisional.
unlocks: Return on investment; Closing-line value; The staking half of the leaderboard; Gate G06; Every reward; Demotion triggers D04, D05 and D06
cost: High. Needs a rights decision and a capture routine, not just code.
risk: NFL.com terms section 1.3 restricts systematic retrieval and commercial use without written consent. Proceeding without consent would put the whole project outside its own stated terms.
acceptance_test: At least one market in price-snapshots.csv carries both an OPEN and a CLOSE row, verified yes, with an operator, a pre-kickoff capture timestamp and a source URL on a registered host; and the leaderboard staking table has at least one row.

title: Retrieve official per-game player logs
problem: The entire player-props division is blocked, and a replacement depth cannot be turned into a value without usage data.
evidence: 0 player-prop correlations could be computed. 2 leaderboard entries are blocked on this alone, and both of them sit in the player-props division.
unlocks: Both player-prop strategies; Correlation C09; Weighting a replacement by actual usage rather than by printed rank
cost: Medium. One page type to identify and register, then a capture pass.
risk: Same rights question as SG-01. Also a volume question: 32 clubs over 10 weeks is a large capture to do at human pace.
acceptance_test: C09 carries a value with a published n, and PP-01 and PP-02 leave the Blocked tier with graded samples.

title: Close the game-status gap in the injury report
problem: A replacement is only implied where the league states an absence, and it states one on a small fraction of rows.
evidence: 25 of 326 injury rows carry a game status; the other 301 carry only a practice status.
unlocks: A complete depth table; Question Q09; Any defensive or offensive deficiency measure that is not a floor
cost: Low to medium. Either find the field on a page not yet read, or record the absence as the finding.
risk: The league may simply not publish it for those players. In that case the right answer is to publish the ceiling, which is what this lab already does.
acceptance_test: Either 90% of injury rows carry a game status, or a second official source states availability, or the gap is published on the flagged page with the page that was checked.

title: Reconcile the two directional records on one frozen forecast table
problem: Two desks publish a directional record for the same season and disagree, and a reader has no way to tell which to trust.
evidence: This desk records 70-120 (0.5833), the earlier results desk records 77-43 (0.6417). A sensitivity run shows the home allowance is not the cause: forcing this model to two points gives 62-120 (0.5167), which is further away, not closer.
unlocks: Question Q18; A single reference model for the board
cost: Low. Both models are in the repository already.
risk: Low. The outcome is a published difference, not a forced agreement.
acceptance_test: One frozen forecast table, both models graded on it in the same run, and the difference published with each model's formula.

title: Extend the results feed every week and re-run the reconciliation
problem: Sample size is the binding constraint on every skill conclusion in this lab, and it is the one thing that only time fixes.
evidence: 137 settled games today. Detecting a true 60% rate at 80% power needs 153 settled selections; 55% needs 617. The largest strategy sample is 120.
unlocks: Question Q03; Question Q13; Any eventual promotion
cost: Low per week. One page read and one build.
risk: Low. The reconciliation aborts the build on any mismatch, so a bad week cannot pass silently.
acceptance_test: The feed extends by the newly published week and the reconciliation still reports 192 of 192 club fields matching.

title: Record the printed as-of date on every depth chart and drop stale charts
problem: A replacement depth is only as current as the chart it came from, and most captured charts do not print a date.
evidence: Chicago prints a chart dated 10/31/2026, before the injury ledger it is joined to. Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa print no date. Philadelphia's chart is self-labelled unofficial.
unlocks: Question Q20; Trust in the depth table
risk: Dropping charts reduces coverage. The trade is published either way.
acceptance_test: Every captured chart carries either a printed date or an explicit no-date flag, and no chart older than the ledger it joins is used without a flag.

title: Identify the unnamed standings columns from a page that names them
problem: Home, road, division and conference splits are withheld because the rendered table does not say which column is which.
evidence: The page prints three unnamed three-part records and two unnamed decimals. Sixteen displayed fields are withheld across the standings pages.
unlocks: A home and road split; A better home-allowance estimate than the league-wide mean; Question Q17
cost: Low. One read of the conference or league view.
acceptance_test: HOME, ROAD, DIV and CONF are identified, and the values reconcile with the win, loss and tie columns.

title: Keep the signal and staking tables on separate pages with the one-way rule stated on both
problem: A reader who sees a return next to a hit rate will read the return as evidence about the forecast.
evidence: The staking table currently has 0 rows and every staking column is blank by rule.
cost: Low. Already implemented here; the suggestion is to keep it that way when a price arrives.
acceptance_test: No page shows a return, a stake or a drawdown in the same table as a hit rate, and both tables print the rule that staking can demote and never promote.

title: Keep the decision record on the suggestions page manual
problem: A suggestion that is implemented because it was written down is not a decision, it is an accident.
evidence: 20 questions are open or partial; 0 suggestions have been adopted so far.
unlocks: A reviewable path from suggestion to change
risk: None. It is the absence of an action.
acceptance_test: The record starts empty, each row offers Adopt, Defer and Reject with a reason field, and the export contains no choice until a person enters one.

title: Publish the sample-size table next to every skill claim
problem: A 61.7% record looks like an edge until it is placed next to the number of selections needed to call it one.
evidence: 153 selections for a true 60% rate, 617 for 55%, 2,682 for 52.4%. The largest sample here is 120.
unlocks: Honest reading of every number on the site
acceptance_test: Every page that prints a hit rate also prints the selections needed to detect it at 80% power.

title: Keep control entries visibly separated from competitors
problem: A control that scores well will be read as a strategy.
evidence: 2 entries are controls. One of them, the duplicate-leg slip, has the strongest statistics in the whole table precisely because its legs are the same event.
acceptance_test: Controls are unranked, carry a Control tier, and print what property of the test they demonstrate.

title: Settle the source-rights question before building any price capture
problem: Code written before the rights question is answered is code that may have to be deleted.
evidence: NFL.com terms section 1.3 permits individual non-commercial informational use and prohibits systematic retrieval to compile a collection without written consent. No consent is evidenced.
unlocks: SG-01; SG-02; Gate G10; Any dataset release
risk: Doing this second rather than first wastes the work in SG-01 and SG-02.
acceptance_test: A written answer on record: consent obtained, a different source used, or the price work formally declined.
